extracted.intended_audience: heads of executive departments and establishments; federal procurement officials; agency counsel and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register transmittal and final notice rescinding OMB Circular No. A-49 (Use of Management and Operating Contracts), describing the rescission, its effective date, rationale, and where governing guidance now resides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission statement / action
rubrics_metrics.description: This rescission notice is issued to cancel OMB Circular No. A-49, 'Use of Management and Operating Contracts.' Transmittal Memorandum No.1 to OMB Circular No. A-49 is effective as of the date of this notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Register notice must state the agency action (Final notice of rescission), identify the circular by number and title, and explicitly announce that the circular is rescinded and the rescission's effective date. Example language from the page: 'Office of Management and Budget Circular No. 49 is hereby rescinded.'; 'Transmittal Memorandum No.1 to OMB Circular No. A-49, is effective as of the date of this notice.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Where governing policy now resides
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and guidance affecting the use of management and operating contracts is found in the Federal Acquisition Regulation, Subpart 17.6, OFPP Policy Letter 84-1 ('Federally Funded Research and Development Centers'), and in agency implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rescission notice should identify the authoritative replacement sources so agencies know where to look for guidance. Verbatim citation on page: 'Guidance on the use of management and operating contracts is found in the Federal Acquisition Regulation, Subpart 17.6.' and 'Responses ... reaffirmed our assessment that comprehensive guidance currently exists in the Federal Acquisition Regulation, Subpart 17.6, OFPP Policy Letter 84-1 ... and in agency implementing regulations.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale supported by comment responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice explains the basis for rescission: agency comments received in response to the proposed rescission were overwhelmingly supportive and reaffirmed that existing comprehensive guidance made the circular unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a summary of public/agency comments and how those comments support the agency's decision. Example wording: 'Comments received ... were overwhelmingly supportive of that action. Responses from Government agencies reaffirmed our assessment that comprehensive guidance currently exists ... The circular is no longer necessary and is being cancelled.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register notice components (metadata and structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Register notice includes standard headings and metadata: AGENCY, ACTION, SUMMARY, EFFECTIVE, FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT, SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION, signature/date, and FR Doc filing notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting a rescission notice, include the formal FR structure and labels. The page shows: 'AGENCY: Office of Management and Budget, Office of Federal Procurement Policy.'; 'ACTION: Final notice of rescission.'; 'SUMMARY: This rescission notice is issued to cancel OMB Circular No. A-49 ...'; 'EFFECTIVE: ...'; 'FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Mr. Robert C. Bienvenue, Office of Federal Procurement Policy (202) 395-3254.'; and the Dated/Director signature and (FR Doc.) filing line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal memorandum format and addressees
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmittal memorandum elements: office heading, date, 'TO: The heads of executive departments and establishments', 'FROM: [Administrator/Director]', 'SUBJECT: Use of Management and Operating Contracts', and statement rescinding the circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transmittal memorandum should mirror internal agency transmittal format and clearly address the relevant senior officials. Example: 'Executive Office of the President. Office of Management and Budget. Washington, DC ... To the heads of executive departments and establishments. Subject Use of Management and Operating Contracts. Office of Management and Budget Circular No. 49 is hereby rescinded.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a named contact and telephone number for further information (office and phone number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice includes: 'FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Mr. Robert C. Bienvenue, Office of Federal Procurement Policy (202) 395-3254.' Ensure a clear office contact is listed so readers can obtain additional information or clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of replacement policy instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly cite the specific FAR subpart, OFPP policy letters, and agency implementing regulations that serve as replacement or governing guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites 'Federal Acquisition Regulation, Subpart 17.6' and 'OFPP Policy Letter 84-1, "Federally Funded Research and Development Centers", dated April 4, 1984.' A rescission notice should give precise citations to the regulatory or policy authorities now relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting administrative record and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the date of the notice, the date the decision was made/docketed, and the effective date of the rescission in the notice and the transmittal memorandum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice shows dates in the header, Dated: January 27, 1988, and Federal Register publication date: 'Wednesday, February 5, 1986.' Ensure dates and any FR volume/number/page citations are included to establish legal effect and the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement that circular is unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Make an explicit determination that the circular is no longer necessary because comprehensive guidance exists elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice states: 'The circular is no longer necessary and is being cancelled.' A rescission should include an explicit conclusion about necessity or redundancy and the basis for that conclusion (e.g., existence of comprehensive alternative guidance).
